papers_and_learning_resources.title: Smoothness-Integrated Trend Distances with Nonzero Difference Drift
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: This working research note compares complete smoothness-indexed families of penalized least-squares (PLS) trends in a Hilbert-space framework. It permits nonzero reference drift in finite-difference penalties, distinguishes that drift from the signed mean gap between fitted trends, and derives global, rolling-window, and smoothness–time distances with spectral representations for shared and unequal drifts.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: Dynamic Forecast-Optimal Smoothness for Penalized Trend Estimation
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: Develops a framework for tracking multiple local minima of chronological forecast-loss surfaces across forecast origins. Persistent branches retain smoothness, first-stage validation loss, and refitted subsequent loss; branch-selection and branch-to-smoothness rules are evaluated separately. Results favor horizon-matched pooled forecasting in controlled simulations, while broader tests do not establish a universally superior dynamic rule.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: Smoothness-Indexed Penalized Trend Estimation in Python: Parameter-Search Coordinates, Numerical Backends, and Reproducible Comparisons
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: Presents a reproducible Python implementation of Guerrero-style penalized least-squares smoothing with an order-normalized smoothness coordinate. Distinguishes parameter-search coordinate from statistical criterion and compares seven numerical backends in an archived 80,640-record factorial study. Independent paired timing experiments and four root-finding methods examine accuracy and performance, with CO₂ and federal funds examples.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: Posterior Integration and Volatility Inputs in WTI Asian Options
papers_and_learning_resources.status_detail: Blinded research manuscript · Submission not verified
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: Studies whether Bayesian posterior integration changes WTI average-price option values as much as the volatility information supplied to the pricing model. A 10-million-history synthetic experiment separates curvature and posterior-dispersion effects. The original date-ordered sample and a separate settlement-mark benchmark show much lower pricing errors using earlier option-implied volatility than historical-volatility posterior integration under their respective modeling assumptions.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: Componentwise kNN-Isomap: From Neighborhood Graphs to Constrained Manifold Embeddings
papers_and_learning_resources.status_detail: 53-slide mathematical lecture · Not a journal submission
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: A mathematical lecture deriving the graph-shortest-path, classical MDS, and rigid-placement stages of componentwise Isomap. It distinguishes connected-component discovery from independent embedding, states a constructive strip-separation guarantee, and uses completed EXP-010/EXP-011 experiments to illustrate distortion and separation trade-offs. A more ambitious separation-constrained optimization is explicitly proposed, not implemented.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: From Max-Cut to Semidefinite Programming, EVA, and Clustering-Based Rounding
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: A step-by-step mathematical tutorial on weighted Max-Cut, sign and Laplacian formulations, semidefinite relaxation, low-rank unit-vector factorization and Efficient Vector Ascent (EVA). It compares Goemans–Williamson random-hyperplane rounding with two spherical clustering choices, K-Means2N and K-MeansNM, and explains saved-factor reuse, independent rounding restarts, and G-set evaluation.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: Unit-Region Factorization for Empty-Region Proximity Graphs
papers_and_learning_resources.status_detail: Elsevier · Discrete Applied Mathematics · Special Issue LAGOS 2025
papers_and_learning_resources.authors_display: Heriberto Espino Montelongo and Héctor Maravillo
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: A fixed-template empty-region rule assigns a Borel region \(S(p,q)\) to a candidate pair and retains the edge when that region contains no other site. The manuscript isolates the unit-volume constant \(a_K\) for similarity-copy regions and shows how the same scalar controls exact Poisson void probabilities, incident-edge length intensities, mean out-degree, and normalized incident-edge length laws.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: Geometry and Volume of Stepping-Stone Diversion Neighborhoods in Euclidean Spaces of Arbitrary Dimension
papers_and_learning_resources.authors_display: Heriberto Espino Montelongo and Héctor Maravillo
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: This manuscript develops a geometric, graph-theoretic, and probabilistic analysis of the stepping-stone graph in \(\mathbb{R}^d\) for every \(d\geq 2\). It derives a normalized one-dimensional volume integral, recovers the degenerate and Gabriel cases and the relative-neighborhood limit, proves strict region and volume monotonicity, establishes graph inclusions and connectivity, and validates a stable quadrature formula by rejection sampling.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: Beyond the Incentive Threshold: Academic Support Use and Persistence After a First-Year Participation Incentive
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: A longitudinal study of \(n=3{,}241\) students examining whether formal mathematics-support use persists from an incentive-linked first-year context into later Calculus I use after that same incentive context is no longer assumed to apply.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: When Do Activation-Patching Effects Add Up? Evidence from Controlled CNNs
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: This study asks when the effects of joint activation-channel patches can be predicted by summing individual channel changes. In controlled convolutional networks, intervention-size effects can occur even under exact logit additivity; other architectures exhibit substantial departures that can reverse a training-regime contrast.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: Mathematics Support Use and Classroom-Relative Performance in First-Year University Mathematics
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: An observational study of \(n=6{,}627\) first-year mathematics students linking same-period mathematics-support use to classroom-relative academic performance while keeping self-selection and non-causal interpretation explicit.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: Are Course Grades Comparable Across Classrooms? Instructor-by-Term Heterogeneity in Undergraduate Mathematics Assessment
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: A measurement study of classroom-level grade heterogeneity in undergraduate mathematics, asking whether a common numerical grade \(g\) can be treated as empirically exchangeable across instructor-by-term contexts.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: From Assigned to Chosen Academic Contexts: Longitudinal Traces of Student Engagement and Adaptation in First-Year University Mathematics
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: An administrative-data study of \(n=6{,}627\) students that distinguishes academic context, experienced performance, formal help-seeking, later context selection, and subsequent outcomes. The analysis identifies five first-course states, examines later Calculus enrolment, and follows adaptation after failed first-course attempts while keeping the findings descriptive rather than causal.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: Template Priors in Small CNNs: Learning Dynamics and the Measurement Dependence of Causal Usefulness
papers_and_learning_resources.status_detail: Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR) · Double-blind review
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: A controlled study of template initialization, retention, and release in small CNNs on two rendering tasks. Across staged experiments with \(n=400\) primary runs, \(n=200\) gradual-release runs, \(80\) final checkpoints, and \(2{,}000\) saved states, template initialization does not uniformly accelerate learning; releasing retention improves compositional accuracy relative to constant retention while reducing alignment; and the relative causal-usefulness difference changes with channel ranking and intervention size.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: Bayesian Parameter Uncertainty in WTI Average Price Option Valuation
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: A working study of Bayesian parameter uncertainty in WTI average-price option valuation. It separates statistical learning under the physical measure from no-arbitrage valuation under the risk-neutral measure and propagates posterior uncertainty in volatility into arithmetic-average option prices. The empirical design combines \(213\) unique call and put contracts with \(11{,}179\) option-date observations spanning September 2026 to June 2029.

papers_and_learning_resources.title: A Reproducible Comparison of Trend Estimation Methods on S&P 500 Log Prices
papers_and_learning_resources.summary: Empirical comparison of train-validation smoothness selection for penalized trends (\widehat{t}(\lambda)) against time-weighted validation and benchmark methods on S&P 500 log prices. The design uses a strict temporal train/validation/test protocol and separates Guerrero smoothness from realized roughness diagnostics.

projects.title: Dinámicas Espaciales en la Incidencia de Robos en la Ciudad de México en 2024

The bivariate theft–homicide association is reported as \(I=0.11\) with \(p=0.205\), while local results distinguish HH, LH, LL, and non-significant areas.

projects.title: Implementación de un Algoritmo Genético para el UFLP
projects.summary: A genetic-algorithm implementation for the uncapacitated facility location problem (UFLP), with the objective of minimizing total operating and assignment cost. It compares four configurations while fixing population size \(N=100\) and maximum generations \(G=30\) during hyperparameter tuning.

projects.title: Right-Censored Regression for IBD with CatBoost and XGBoost Stacking
projects.summary: A censor-aware stacking pipeline for an IBD target right-censored at \(c=20\). CatBoost is trained on uncensored cases using \(K=9\)-fold out-of-fold predictions, a robust residual scale is estimated, and Tobit-style tail corrections are applied before XGBoost meta-learning.

projects.title: Proximity Graphs
projects.summary: A poster presenting a Python API for constructing, visualizing, and comparing proximity-graph families and biologically inspired models. It connects an empty-region area \(A(\ell)=w\ell^2\) with Poisson edge-survival probabilities and asymptotic graph properties.

projects.title: Proximity Graphs: Construction and Asymptotic Characteristics
projects.summary: A poster on proximity-graph construction and asymptotic characteristics, including explicit area formulas for the β-lune and stepping-stone diversion kernels. For a Poisson process, it presents the empty-neighbourhood relation \(\Pr(\mathrm{empty})=e^{-\rho w\ell^2}\) and its connection to asymptotic expected degree.

notes.title: Random Variables as Vectors: Geometry of L², Projections, Variance, and Bias
notes.summary: In-progress notes formalizing random variables as vectors in the Hilbert space \(L^2(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})\). They interpret expectation and conditional expectation as orthogonal projections, variance and bias-variance as Pythagorean decompositions, and Chapman-Kolmogorov as a tower-property identity.

Research Drafts.subtitle: Smoothness-Integrated Trend Distances with Nonzero Difference Drift
highlights: Working research note; not submitted to a journal.
Defined Hilbert-space distances across normalized smoothness-indexed PLS trend families with nonzero finite-difference reference drift.
Derived shared/unequal-drift spectral formulas, signed level-versus-shape decompositions, and rolling smoothness–time dissimilarity measures.
Proposed agricultural index monitoring applications while identifying retrospective-data leakage and validation requirements.

Research Drafts.name: Dynamic Forecast-Optimal Smoothness for Penalized Trend Estimation
highlights: Tracked multiple forecast-loss minima through chronological origins and distinguished persistent-branch selection from mapping each branch to a current smoothness decision.
Evaluated pooled versus dynamic selection in simulations and financial data; observed mixed evidence, without claiming universal forecasting superiority.

Research Drafts.name: Smoothness-Indexed Penalized Trend Estimation in Python: Parameter-Search Coordinates, Numerical Backends, and Reproducible Comparisons
highlights: Coauthored with Daniela Cortés-Toto; implemented normalized Guerrero smoothness and compared seven PLS numerical backends.
Documented 80,640 archived computational records, independently paired timing experiments, and numerical root-finding validation.

Research Drafts.name: Posterior Integration and Volatility Inputs in WTI Asian Options
highlights: Separated Bayesian posterior-integration corrections from the volatility information used for WTI average-price option pricing.
Combined a 10-million-history simulation with distinct date-ordered and settlement-mark empirical samples, emphasizing prior implied volatility and experimental limitations.

Research Drafts.name: Componentwise kNN-Isomap: From Neighborhood Graphs to Constrained Manifold Embeddings
highlights: Prepared a 53-slide derivation covering graph geodesics, classical MDS, componentwise unfolding, and guaranteed strip separation.
Used EXP-010/EXP-011 observations and distinguished the proposed separation-constrained placement optimizer from implemented methods.

Research Drafts.name: From Max-Cut to Semidefinite Programming, EVA, and Clustering-Based Rounding
highlights: Explained SDP relaxations of Max-Cut, low-rank Efficient Vector Ascent (EVA), and hyperplane versus spherical K-Means rounding.
Documented matched rounding restarts, G-set reproducibility, and the distinction between Max-Cut and general Max-k-Cut.

Research Drafts.name: Bayesian Uncertainty in WTI Options
highlights: Studied the propagation of posterior parameter uncertainty into WTI option valuation.

Research Drafts.name: Mathematical Notes on Random Variables as Vectors in L²
highlights: Wrote formal L² notes framing random variables as Hilbert-space vectors, with expectation, variance, MSE, bias–variance, and regression error as projections.
Derived conditional expectation, tower property, Chapman–Kolmogorov, and total variance as nested projection identities in L² with geometric diagrams and examples.
